properties.areaDesc: Hardin, TX; Jefferson, TX
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 8 at 11:01AM CDT until September 9 at 8:20PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Hardin and Jefferson
Counties.

...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in
Texas...

Neches River at Neches River Saltwater Barrier affecting Hardin,
Jasper, Orange and Jefferson Counties.

For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Pine Island Bayou near Sour Lake.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 25.0 feet, Water inundates roads in lowland areas near
the river. Low spots on Old Sour Lake Road are under water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:45 AM CDT Tuesday the stage was 26.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:45 AM CDT Tuesday was 27.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow morning and continue falling to 19.4 feet Sunday
morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 26.7
feet on 04/24/1977.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 1215 PM CDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL WEDNESDAY EVENING

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued September 8 at 5:17AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
HLSHFO

This product covers the Hawaiian islands

**HURRICANE LOWELL BEGINNING TO MOVE AWAY**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Hurricane Warning is in effect for Kauai East, Kauai
Mountains, Kauai North, Kauai South, Kauai Southwest, and Niihau
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Central Oahu, East
Honolulu, Ewa Plain, Honolulu Metro, Koolau Leeward, Koolau
Windward, Oahu North Shore, Olomana, Waianae Coast, and Waianae
Mountains

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 150 miles northwest of Lihue or about 240 miles northwest
of Honolulu
- 23.7N 160.7W
- Storm Intensity 90 mph
- Movement North or 360 degrees at 18 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Hurricane Lowell has reached its closest point to the main Hawaiian
Islands around midnight and will begin moving away from the islands
this morning. However, this is not the time to let your guard down.
Damaging winds, heavy flooding rainfall, and extremely dangerous and
damaging surf will occur across the Hawaiian Islands at least through
the morning, and possibly through the day. A Hurricane Warning remains
in effect for Kauai and Niihau, and a Tropical Storm Warning for Oahu.

Current wind gusts appear to be in the 40 to 50 mph range on Kauai,
and 30 to 40 mph range on Oahu. It is important to note that winds can be
accelerated over and downwind of terrain, leading to areas of stronger
wind gusts. Winds will rapidly drop of by this afternoon.

Heavy downpours could lead to flash flooding on already saturated
grounds. Lingering rain bands will continue into Wednesday as Lowell
lifts away to the north and drags additonal tropical moisture in the
southerly flow. Additional rainfall for this event are 2 to 4 inches
on Kauai, 1 to 2 inches on Oahu and Maui County, and 3 to 6 inches on
Big Island with higher amounts occurring on south and eastern slopes.

A large south to southwest swell iwill continue this morning with
heights of 15 to 20 feet across south and west facing shores of Kauai
and 10 to 14 feet across the remaining south and west shorelines. Surf
is forecast to rapidly drop off by this afternoon.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
Kauai and Niihau. Remain well sheltered from dangerous
wind having possible significant impacts. If realized, these impacts
include:
- Structural damage to sturdy buildings, some with complete roof
and wall failures. Complete destruction of mobile homes. Damage
greatly accentuated by large airborne projectiles. Locations
may be uninhabitable for weeks or months.
- Numerous large trees snapped or uprooted along with fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- Many roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places. Many bridges, causeways, and access
routes impassable.
- Widespread power and communications outages.

Potential impacts from the main wind event are also now unfolding
across Oahu. Remain well sheltered from wind having limited to
extensive impacts.

Elsewhere across the Hawaiian islands, little to no impact is
anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Potential impacts from the flooding rain are unfolding across Kauai
and Niihau. Remain well guarded against life-threatening flood waters
having extensive impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, arroyos, and
ditches may become dangerous rivers. In mountain areas,
destructive runoff may run quickly down valleys while
increasing susceptibility to rockslides and mudslides. Flood
control systems and barriers may become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Potential impacts from the flooding rain are unfolding across the
rest of the State of Hawaii. Remain well guarded against dangerous
flood waters having significant impacts.

* SURGE:
Little to no additional impacts are anticipated at this time
across the Hawaiian islands.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to stay inside and away from windows. Listen for
updates and be ready in case you lose electrical power. Keep a
battery-powered radio, charged cell phone and flashlight handy.

During the peak of the storm be ready to move quickly. Keep your
shoes on and rain gear handy. Boots and athletic shoes offer the
best foot protection if you become unexpectedly exposed to the
weather.

Failure to adequately shelter may result in serious injury or loss of
life. Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with any
orders that are issued. Remember, during the storm 9 1 1 Emergency
Services may not be able to immediately respond if conditions are
unsafe. This should be a big factor in your decision making.

If you are a visitor, be sure to know the name of the city or town in
which you are staying and the name of the county or parish in which
it resides. Listen for these locations in local news updates. Pay
attention for instructions from local authorities.

Keep your cell phone charged and in power-saving mode. If you lose
power, use it sparingly and mainly for personal emergencies and
check-ins.

If you are prone to flooding be prepared for the possibility of a
quick and dramatic rise in water levels.


* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Honolulu HI around 8 AM HST, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

properties.description:
...HIGH SURF WARNING FOR SOUTH FACING SHORES OF ALL ISLANDS
TODAY...
...HIGH SURF WARNING FOR WEST FACING SHORES OF BIG ISLAND
TODAY...
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY FOR EAST FACING SHORES OF ALL
ISLANDS TODAY...

.Southwest swell from Hurricane Lowell produced surf along south
facing shores in excess of warning criteria overnight. This surf
continues into the early morning hours, which may continue to
bring damaging surf to portions of Kauai County with the
potential for significant damage to coastal properties and
infrastructure, particularly to those areas along the coast
exposed to the southerly swell over the next several hours. Surf
will quickly fall to advisory criteria and then below advisory
criteria by tonight.

A medium-period east swell from former Tropical Storm Karina combined
with east to southeast wind wave generated by Hurricane Lowell will
maintain advisory level surf along east facing shores this morning,
but will drop below advisory levels by tonight.

* WHAT...Surf 20 to 30 feet rapidly declining through the day,
becoming 6 to 8 feet by this afternoon.

* WHERE...South facing shores of Kauai and Niihau.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Extreme...Expect ocean water surging and sweeping
over beaches, coastal benches, and roadways, creating the
potential for significant damage to coastal properties and
infrastructure, including roadways. Coastal evacuations and
road closures are possible. Large breaking waves may affect
harbor entrances and channels with significant damage possible
to docks, piers, ramps, and boats.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Vulnerable coastal roadways from Poipu to
Kekaha are susceptible to overwash, with Lawai Road at a
particular risk for overwash.
properties.instruction:
Stay away from the shoreline along the affected coasts. Be
prepared for road closures. Postpone entering or leaving channels
affected by the high surf until the surf subsides.

properties.description:
HLSHFO

This product covers the Hawaiian islands

**HURRICANE LOWELL MADE CLOSEST ENCOUNTER TO HAWAII AROUND MIDNIGHT AND
IS NOW BEGINNING TO MOVE AWAY**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Hurricane Warning is in effect for Kauai East, Kauai
Mountains, Kauai North, Kauai South, Kauai Southwest, and Niihau
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Central Oahu, East
Honolulu, Ewa Plain, Honolulu Metro, Koolau Leeward, Koolau
Windward, Oahu North Shore, Olomana, Waianae Coast, and Waianae
Mountains

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 110 miles northwest of Lihue or about 210 miles
west-northwest of Honolulu
- 22.9N 160.8W
- Storm Intensity 105 mph
- Movement North or 10 degrees at 18 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Hurricane Lowell has reached its closest point to the main Hawaiian
Islands around midnight and will begin moving away from the islands
this morning. However, this is not the time to let your guard down.
Damaging winds, heavy flooding rainfall, and extremely dangerous and
damaging surf will occur across the Hawaiian Islands at least through
the morning, and possibly through the day. A Hurricane Warning remains
in effect for Kauai and Niihau, and a Tropical Storm Warning for Oahu.

Peak wind gusts across Kauai and Oahu over the past few hours were as
high as 80 mph. Current wind gusts appear to be slightly off the peak,
but still holding steady in the 60 to 70 mph range on Kauai, and 30 to
50 mph range on Oahu. It is important to note that winds can be
accelerated over and downwind of terrain, leading to areas of stronger
wind gusts. As winds turn southward, north facing slopes will be more
susceptable to downsloping effects.

Heavy downpours could lead to flash flooding on already saturated
grounds. Lingering rain bands will continue into Wednesday as Lowell
lifts away to the north and drags additonal tropical moisture in the
southerly flow. Additional rainfall for this event are 2 to 4 inches
on Kauai, 1 to 2 inches on Oahu and Maui County, and 3 to 6 inches
on Big Island with higher amounts occurring on south and eastern slopes.

An extremely large south to southwest swell is currently peaking with
heights of 20 to 30 feet across south and west facing shores of Kauai
and 15 to 20 feet same shorelines of Oahu. Surf is forecast to rapidly
diminish this morning, but will likely maintain the warning through
the morning for south and west facing shores. Storm surge of 1 to
4 feet on Kauai and Niihau will generate major wave run-up and coastal
inundation along exposed low lying areas of south and west- facing
shores.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
Kauai and Niihau. Remain well sheltered from life-threatening wind
impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Structural damage to sturdy buildings, some with complete roof
and wall failures. Complete destruction of mobile homes. Damage
greatly accentuated by large airborne projectiles. Locations
may be uninhabitable for weeks or months.
- Numerous large trees snapped or uprooted along with fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- Many roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places. Many bridges, causeways, and access
routes impassable.
- Widespread power and communications outages.

Potential impacts from the main wind event will develop across Oahu
this evening. Remain well sheltered from wind having limited to
extensive impacts.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Potential impacts from the flooding rain are unfolding across Kauai
and Niihau. Remain well guarded against life-threatening flood waters
having extensive impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, arroyos, and
ditches may become dangerous rivers. In mountain areas,
destructive runoff may run quickly down valleys while
increasing susceptibility to rockslides and mudslides. Flood
control systems and barriers may become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Potential impacts from the flooding rain are unfolding across the
rest of the State of Hawaii. Remain well guarded against dangerous
flood waters having significant impacts.

* SURGE:
Potential impacts from the main surge and damaging surf event are now
unfolding across Kauai and Niihau. Remain well away from
life-threatening surge and extremely large surf having significant
impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Areas of inundation with storm surge flooding accentuated by
waves. Damage to several buildings, mainly near the coast.
- Sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads become
weakened or washed out, especially in usually vulnerable low
spots.
- Major beach erosion with heavy surf overtopping nearby roadways.
- Moderate damage to marinas, docks, and piers. Several small
craft broken away from moorings, especially in unprotected
anchorages.

Elsewhere across the Hawaiian islands, very large surf may produce
coastal inundation and some impacts to shoreline infrastructure.

* TORNADOES:
Potential impacts from tornadoes are unfolding across Kauai and
Niihau. Remain well braced against a dangerous tornado event having
possible significant impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- The occurrence of scattered tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- Several places may experience tornado damage with a few spots
of considerable damage, power loss, and communications failures.
- Locations could realize roofs torn off frame houses, mobile
homes demolished, boxcars overturned, large trees snapped or
uprooted, vehicles tumbled, and small boats tossed about.
Dangerous projectiles can add to the toll.

Prepare for a tornado event having possible limited impacts across
the rest of the State of Hawaii.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to stay inside and away from windows. Listen for
updates and be ready in case you lose electrical power. Keep a
battery-powered radio, charged cell phone and flashlight handy.

During the peak of the storm be ready to move quickly. Keep your
shoes on and rain gear handy. Boots and athletic shoes offer the
best foot protection if you become unexpectedly exposed to the
weather.

Failure to adequately shelter may result in serious injury or loss of
life. Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with any
orders that are issued. Remember, during the storm 9 1 1 Emergency
Services may not be able to immediately respond if conditions are
unsafe. This should be a big factor in your decision making.

If you are a visitor, be sure to know the name of the city or town in
which you are staying and the name of the county or parish in which
it resides. Listen for these locations in local news updates. Pay
attention for instructions from local authorities.

Keep your cell phone charged and in power-saving mode. If you lose
power, use it sparingly and mainly for personal emergencies and
check-ins.

If you are prone to flooding be prepared for the possibility of a
quick and dramatic rise in water levels.

If a tornado warning is issued for your area, quickly move to the
safest place within your shelter. Protect your head and body.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Honolulu HI around 5 AM HST, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

heat stroke.

possible.

* WHERE...A portion of north central Montana, including the following
areas, East Glacier Park Region, Eastern Glacier, Western Toole,
and Central Pondera, Eastern Pondera and Eastern Teton, Eastern
Toole and Liberty, Northern High Plains, Southern High Plains and
Southern Rocky Mountain Front.

* WHEN...Until noon MDT today.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in minor flooding of creeks,

may occur in poor drainage areas. Rural gravel and dirt roads can
become muddy and may become difficult to travel. Rock/debris slides
are possible in the mountains.

- Periods of rain through this morning could result in minor
flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued September 7 at 10:58PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
HLSHFO

This product covers the Hawaiian islands

**HURRICANE LOWELL AT ITS CLOSEST POINT TO HAWAII**


NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Hurricane Warning is in effect for Kauai East, Kauai
Mountains, Kauai North, Kauai South, Kauai Southwest, and Niihau
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Central Oahu, East
Honolulu, Ewa Plain, Honolulu Metro, Koolau Leeward, Koolau
Windward, Oahu North Shore, Olomana, Waianae Coast, and Waianae
Mountains

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 140 miles west-southwest of Lihue or about 210 miles west
of Honolulu
- 20.9N 161.1W
- Storm Intensity 110 mph
- Movement North-northeast or 25 degrees at 18 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Hurricane Lowell has reached its closest point to the main Hawaiian
Islands. Expect damaging winds, heavy flooding rainfall, and extremely
dangerous and damaging surf to occur over portions of the Hawaiian
Islands and into Tuesday morning. A Hurricane Warning remains in effect
for Kauai and Niihau, and a Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for
Oahu. Storm preparations should be complete.

Damaging winds are now occurring on Kauai, Niihau and Oahu. Wind gust
reports since midday show highest values across Oahu and Kauai County
from 50 to 80 mph, with peak winds expected to last for a few more
hours tonight. It is important to note that winds can be accelerated
over and downwind of terrain, leading to areas of stronger wind gusts.
As winds shift to south overnight, areas affected by downslope wind
gusts will likely change.

Heavy downpours could lead to flash flooding and mudslides, especially in
steep terrain, and rainbands could become persistent and anchored in
some areas, exacerbating the flash flood threat. The risk of flash
flooding is greatest for Kauai and Niihau, where many stations have
measured 2 to 10 inches of rain with higher values in the upper
elevations. The flood threat also exists for all other islands due
to deep moisture surrounding Lowell. Over 20 inches of storm total
rain is possible over portions of Kauai, mainly over the interior
mountains, and up 12 inches remains possible over southeast Big Island.

An extremely large south to southwest swell generated by Lowell will
continue to rapidly build through the evening and peak tonight. A High
Surf Warning is in effect for south-facing shores of all islands and
for west-facing shores of the Big Island. Dangerously large and
damaging surf and coastal inundation are expected along the immediate
coast of exposed south and west-facing shores, particularly on Kauai
and Niihau and possibly Oahu. The highest surf may reach 20 to 30 feet
on Kauai and Niihau tonight, then rapidly diminish on Tuesday. Extra
large surf, on top of 1 to 4 feet of storm surge, will generate major
wave run-up and coastal inundation along exposed low lying areas of
south and west-facing shores, particularly for Kauai and Niihau and
possibly for Oahu.

Conditions will be conducive for fast-moving, short-lived waterspouts
and tornadoes in the rainbands associated with Lowell, mainly near
Kauai and Niihau. This threat will continue through tonight, then
diminish quickly Tuesday morning.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
Kauai and Niihau. Remain well sheltered from life-threatening wind
impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Structural damage to sturdy buildings, some with complete roof
and wall failures. Complete destruction of mobile homes. Damage
greatly accentuated by large airborne projectiles. Locations
may be uninhabitable for weeks or months.
- Numerous large trees snapped or uprooted along with fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- Many roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places. Many bridges, causeways, and access
routes impassable.
- Widespread power and communications outages.

Potential impacts from the main wind event will develop across Oahu
this evening. Remain well sheltered from wind having limited to
extensive impacts.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Potential impacts from the flooding rain are unfolding across Kauai
and Niihau. Remain well guarded against life-threatening flood waters
having extensive impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, arroyos, and
ditches may become dangerous rivers. In mountain areas,
destructive runoff may run quickly down valleys while
increasing susceptibility to rockslides and mudslides. Flood
control systems and barriers may become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Potential impacts from the flooding rain are unfolding across the
rest of the State of Hawaii. Remain well guarded against dangerous
flood waters having significant impacts.

* SURGE:
Potential impacts from the main surge and damaging surf event are now
unfolding across Kauai and Niihau. Remain well away from
life-threatening surge and extremely large surf having significant
impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Areas of inundation with storm surge flooding accentuated by
waves. Damage to several buildings, mainly near the coast.
- Sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads become
weakened or washed out, especially in usually vulnerable low
spots.
- Major beach erosion with heavy surf overtopping nearby roadways.
- Moderate damage to marinas, docks, and piers. Several small
craft broken away from moorings, especially in unprotected
anchorages.

Elsewhere across the Hawaiian islands, very large surf may produce
coastal inundation and some impacts to shoreline infrastructure.

* TORNADOES:
Potential impacts from tornadoes are unfolding across Kauai and
Niihau. Remain well braced against a dangerous tornado event having
possible significant impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- The occurrence of scattered tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- Several places may experience tornado damage with a few spots
of considerable damage, power loss, and communications failures.
- Locations could realize roofs torn off frame houses, mobile
homes demolished, boxcars overturned, large trees snapped or
uprooted, vehicles tumbled, and small boats tossed about.
Dangerous projectiles can add to the toll.

Prepare for a tornado event having possible limited impacts across
the rest of the State of Hawaii.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to stay inside and away from windows. Listen for
updates and be ready in case you lose electrical power. Keep a
battery-powered radio, charged cell phone and flashlight handy.

During the peak of the storm be ready to move quickly. Keep your
shoes on and rain gear handy. Boots and athletic shoes offer the
best foot protection if you become unexpectedly exposed to the
weather.

Failure to adequately shelter may result in serious injury or loss of
life. Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with any
orders that are issued. Remember, during the storm 9 1 1 Emergency
Services may not be able to immediately respond if conditions are
unsafe. This should be a big factor in your decision making.

If you are a visitor, be sure to know the name of the city or town in
which you are staying and the name of the county or parish in which
it resides. Listen for these locations in local news updates. Pay
attention for instructions from local authorities.

Keep your cell phone charged and in power-saving mode. If you lose
power, use it sparingly and mainly for personal emergencies and
check-ins.

If you are prone to flooding be prepared for the possibility of a
quick and dramatic rise in water levels.

If a tornado warning is issued for your area, quickly move to the
safest place within your shelter. Protect your head and body.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Honolulu HI around 5 AM HST, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 8 at 1:49AM MDT until September 8 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of central New Mexico, including the following
area, South Central Mountains.

* WHEN...From 11 AM MDT this morning through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations
downstream of the South Fork and Salt wildfire burn scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Monsoon moisture and atmospheric instability will be present this
afternoon, leading to the development of strong, slow- moving
thunderstorms over the Sacramento mountains. These slow-moving
storms will be capable of producing rainfall rates of 1 to 2
inches per hour which may lead to excessive runoff on the
vulnerable South Fork and Salt burn scars. These burn scars are
very susceptible to flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 8 at 2:27AM CDT until September 8 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Jackson MS
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 110 degrees expected.

* WHERE...Portions of southeast Arkansas, northeast Louisiana, and
central and western Mississippi.

* WHEN...From 11 AM this morning to 7 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat related
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Riverton has issued a Red Flag
Warning, which is in effect from noon today to 9 PM MDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS: Low Humidities...Strong Gusty Winds...and Wind Shift
with a Cold Front could cause erratic fire behavior.

* AFFECTED AREA:
In Central WY...Fire Weather Zones 280...289 and 300.

* COUNTIES AFFECTED:
In Central WY...Fremont...Natrona.
In Southwest WY...Sweetwater.

* COLD FRONT: Winds will turn more northerly after sunset tonight,
as a cold front comes down from the north.

* WIND: Tuesday - West to southwest 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to
35 mph.

Wednesday - West to southwest 10 to 15 mph with gusts up to 25
mph.

Thursday West to southwest 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 45 mph.

* HUMIDITY: Tuesday - Ranging between 11 to 18 percent.

Wednesday - As low as 8 percent.

Thursday - As low as 7 percent.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now....or will shortly. A combination of strong
winds...low relative humidity...and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

concentrations are expected to reach levels that pose a health risk.
Adverse health effects increase as air quality deteriorates. Ground-
level ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing
difficulties for children, older adults, as well as persons with
respiratory problems.

Reducing outdoor physical activity is recommended. If it is a
regularly scheduled work day you are urged to consider
telecommuting, carpooling, or utilizing public transit. Avoid
excessive idling and do not top off when refueling motor vehicles.
The use of gasoline-powered lawn equipment should be reduced or
postponed until late in the day.

For more information visit the St. Louis Clean Air Partnership at
http://cleanair-stlouis.com/

For current Air Quality Index (AQI) values visit
https://www.airnow.gov/

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 7 at 7:12PM PDT until September 8 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4
to 7 feet with local sets to 8 feet and dangerous and
potentially life threatening rip currents. Highest waves on
south- facing shores of Los Angeles County.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents will be widespread and very strong, potentially pulling
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause
injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small
boats near shore. Significant beach erosion will occur. Flooding
of sea water is likely, around the time of high tide, over
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas such as parking lots,
beaches, walkways, and low-lying roads. Of particular concern
will be the Alamitos Peninsula area in Long Beach where coastal
flooding will potentially cause local damage to structures near
time of high tides. Other areas that will be susceptible to
coastal flooding during the next couple of days include Catalina
Island, and Oxnard to Malibu (including Point Mugu).

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides occurred around 7 feet at 7 pm
today and will be 7.2 feet at 8 pm on Tuesday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 11 PM PDT TUESDAY... ...HIGH SURF ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 11 PM PDT TUESDAY

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous and potentially life threatening rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches, Santa Barbara County
Central Coast Beaches, Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast
and Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents will be widespread and very strong, potentially
pulling swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people
off beaches and rocks. Pooling of sea water is possible around
high tide at beach areas that is uncommon with normal tidal
ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible. No
significant damage is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will occur around 6.5 feet at
730pm today and 6.5 feet at 830pm on Tuesday.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued September 7 at 5:53PM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
The St. Louis Clean Air Partnership has issued an air quality alert
for the St. Louis metropolitan area from 10 AM to 8 PM CDT Tuesday.

An Orange air quality forecast means that maximum ozone
concentrations are expected to reach levels that pose a health risk.
Adverse health effects increase as air quality deteriorates. Ground-
level ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing
difficulties for children, older adults, as well as persons with
respiratory problems.

Reducing outdoor physical activity is recommended. If it is a
regularly scheduled work day you are urged to consider
telecommuting, carpooling, or utilizing public transit. Avoid
excessive idling and do not top off when refueling motor vehicles.
The use of gasoline-powered lawn equipment should be reduced or
postponed until late in the day.

For more information visit the St. Louis Clean Air Partnership at
http://cleanair-stlouis.com/

For current Air Quality Index (AQI) values visit
https://www.airnow.gov/
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 7 at 10:27AM PDT until September 10 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with temperatures 10 to 20 degrees above
normal.

* WHERE...Bay Area and Central Coast.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Wednesday to 10 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration. Impacts possible in some health systems and in
heat-sensitive industries. Hot conditions can cause heat illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Hydration is a critical piece to surviving the heat. Drink water, and
if possible, take water to those who are vulnerable.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to the early
morning or evening. Take action when you experience symptoms of heat
exhaustion and/or heat stroke.

Beat the heat and check the backseat! Do not leave young children or
pets in unattended vehicles. Car interiors will reach lethal
temperatures in a matter of minutes.
